The Ocean is so called because gems are found in its depths. As the Lord has taken the form of the ocean, He is called by this name.
One who is the Lord of all wealth.

verses.devanagari: धर्मगुब्धर्मकृद्धर्मी सदसत्क्षरमक्षरम् । अविज्ञाता सहस्रांशुर्विधाता कृतलक्षणः ॥ ५१ ॥
verses.iast: dharmagubdharmakṛddharmī sadasatkṣaramakṣaram, avijñātā sahasrāṁśurvidhātā kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ.

words.meaning: One who protects Dharma.
Though above. Dharma and Adharma, He performs Dharma in order to keep up the traditions in respect of it.
One who upholds Dharma.
The Parabrahman who is of the nature of truth.
As the Aparabrahma has manifested as the world He is called Asat (not having reality).
All beings subjected to change.
The changeless one.
One who is without the attributes of a Jiva or vigyata like sense of agency, etc.
One with numerous rays, that is the Sun.
One who is the unique support of all agencies like Ananta who bear the whole universe.
One who is of the nature of conscousness.

verses.devanagari: गभस्तिनेमिः सत्त्वस्थः सिंहो भूतमहेश्वरः । आदिदेवो महादेवो देवेशो देवभृद्गुरुः ॥ ५२ ॥
verses.iast: gabhastinemiḥ sattvasthaḥ siṁhō bhūtamaheśvaraḥ, ādidevō mahādevō deveśō devabhṛdguruḥ.

words.meaning: He who dwells in the middle of Gabhasti or rays as the Sun.
One who dwells specially in sattvaguna, which is luminous by nature.
One who ahs irresistible power like a lion.
The supreme Lord of all beings.
He who is the first of all beings.
One whose greatness consists in His supreme self-knowledge.
One who is the lord of all Devas, being the most important among them.
Indra who governs the Devas is Devabhrut. The Lord is even that Indra's controller (Guru).

verses.devanagari: उत्तरो गोपतिर्गोप्ता ज्ञानगम्यः पुरातनः । शरीरभूतभृद्भोक्ता कपीन्द्रो भूरिदक्षिणः ॥ ५३ ॥
verses.iast: uttarō gōpatirgōptā jñānagamyaḥ purātanaḥ, śarīrabhūtabhṛdbhōktā kapīndrō bhūridakṣiṇaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is Uttirna or liberated from Samsara.
Krishna who tends the cattle in the form of a Gopa. One who is the master of the earth.
One who is the protector of all beings.
The Lord cannot be known through Karma or a combination of Karma and Jyana.
One who is not limited by time and who existed before anything else.
One who is the master of the five Bhutas (elements) of which the body is made.
One who protects. Or one who is the enjoyer of infinite bliss.

Kapi means Varah (boar). The word means, the Lord who is Indra and also one who manifested as Varaha or the Boar in one of the incarnations. Or it signifies His Rama incarnation in which He played the role of the master of the monkeys.
One to whom numerous Dakshinas or votive offerings are made in Yajnas.

verses.devanagari: सोमपोऽमृतपः सोमः पुरुजित् पुरुसत्तमः । विनयो जयः सत्यसन्धो दाशार्हस्सात्वतां पतिः ॥ ५४ ॥
verses.iast: somapo’mṛtapaḥ sōmaḥ purujit purusattamaḥ, vinayō jayaḥ satyasandhō dāśārhassātvatāṁ patiḥ.

words.meaning: One who drinks the Soma in all Yajnas in the form of the Devata.
One who drinks the drink of immortal Bliss which is of one's own nature.
One who as the moon invigorates the plants.
One who gains victory over numerous people.
As His form is of cosmic dimension He is Puru or great, and as He is the most important of all, He is Sattama.
One who inflicts Vinaya or punishment on evil ones.
One who is victorious over all beings.
One whose 'Sandha' or resolve becomes always true.
Dasha means charitable offering. Therefore, He to whom charitable offerings deserve to be made.
'Satvatam' is the name of a Tantra. So the one who gave it out or commented upon it.

verses.devanagari: जीवो विनयिता साक्षी मुकुन्दोऽमितविक्रमः । अम्भोनिधिरनन्तात्मा महोदधिशयोऽन्तकः ॥ ५५ ॥
verses.iast: jīvo vinayitā sākṣī mukundo’mitavikramaḥ, ambhonidhiranantātmā mahodadhiśayo’ntakaḥ.

words.meaning: One who as the Kshetragya or knower of the field or the body, is associated with the Pranas.
One who witnesses the Vinayita or worshipful attitude of all devotees.
One who bestows Mukti or Liberation.
One whose three strides were limitless.
One in whom the Ambas or all beings from Devas down dwell.
One who cannot be determined by space, time and causation.
One who lies in the water of Cosmic Dissolution into which all entities in the universe have been dissolved.
One who brings about the end of all beings.

verses.devanagari: अजो महार्हः स्वाभाव्यो जितामित्रः प्रमोदनः । आनन्दो नन्दनो नन्दः सत्यधर्मा त्रिविक्रमः ॥ ५६ ॥
verses.iast: ajō mahārhaḥ svābhāvyō jitāmitraḥ pramōdanaḥ, ānandō nandanō nandaḥ satyadharmā trivikramaḥ.

words.meaning: 'A' means Mahavishnu. So the word means one who is born of Vishnu i.e. Kama Deva.
One who is fit for worship.
Being eternally perfect He is naturally without a beginning.
One who has conquered the inner enemies like attachment, anger, etc. as also external enemies like Ravana, Kumbhakarna etc.
One who is always joyous as He is absorbed in immortal Bliss.
One whose form is Ananda or Bliss.
One who gives delight.
One endowed with all perfections.
One whose knowledge and other attributes are true.
One whose three strides covered the whole world.

verses.devanagari: महर्षिः कपिलाचार्यः कृतज्ञो मेदिनीपतिः । त्रिपदस्त्रिदशाध्यक्षो महाशृङ्गः कृतान्तकृत् ॥ ५७ ॥
verses.iast: maharṣiḥ kapilācāryaḥ kṛtajñō medinīpatiḥ, tripadastridaśādhyakṣō mahāśṛṅgaḥ kṛtāntakṛt.

words.meaning: Kapila is called Maharshi because he was master of all the Vedas.
Kruta means the world because it is of the nature of an effect.
One who is the Lord of the earth.
One having three strides.
One who is the witness of the three states of waking, dream and sleep, which spring from the influence of the Gunas.
One with a great antenna.
One who brings about the destruction of the Kruta or the manifested condition of the universe.

verses.devanagari: महावराहो गोविन्दः सुषेणः कनकाङ्गदी । गुह्यो गभीरो गहनो गुप्तश्चक्रगदाधरः ॥ ५८ ॥
verses.iast: mahāvarāhō gōvindaḥ suṣeṇaḥ kanakāṅgadī, guhyō gabhīrō gahanō guptaścakragadādharaḥ.

words.meaning: The great Cosmic Boar.
'Go' means Words, that is the Vedic sentences. He who is known by them is Gōvindaḥ.
One who has got about Him an armed guard in the shape of His eternal associates.
One who has Angadas (armlets) made of gold.
One who is to be known by the Guhya or the esoteric knowledge conveyed by the Upanishads. Or one who is hidden in the Guha or heart.
One who is of profound majesty because of attributes like omniscience, lordliness, strength, prowess, etc.
One who could be entered into only with great difficulty. One who is the witness of the three states of waking, dreams and sleep as also their absence.
One who is not an object of words, thought, etc.
One who has discus and Gada in hand.

verses.devanagari: वेधाः स्वाङ्गोऽजितः कृष्णो दृढः सङ्कर्षणोऽच्युतः । वरुणो वारुणो वृउक्षः पुष्कराक्षो महामनाः ॥ ५९ ॥
verses.iast: vedhāḥ svāṅgo’jitaḥ kṛṣṇo dṛḍhaḥ saṅkarṣaṇo’cyutaḥ, varuṇo vāruṇo vṛukṣaḥ puṣkarākṣo mahāmanāḥ.

words.meaning: One who does Vidhana or regulation.
One who is oneself the participant in accomplishing works.
One who has not been conquered by anyone in His various incarnations.
One who is known as Krishna-dvaipayana.
One whose nature and capacity know no decay.

Sankarshana is one who attracts to oneself all beings at the time of cosmic Dissolution and Acyuta is one who knows no fall from His real nature. They form one word with the first as the qualification – Acyuta who is Sankarshana.
The evening sun is called Varuna, because he withdraws his rays into himself.
Vasishta or Agastya, the sons of Varuna.
One who is unshakable like a tree.
One who shines as the light of consciousness when meditated upon in the lotus of the heart. Or one who has eyes resembling the lotus.
One who fulfils the three functions of creation, sustentation and dissolution of the universe by the mind alone.

verses.devanagari: भगवान् भगहानन्दी वनमाली हलायुधः । आदित्यो ज्योतिरादित्यः सहिष्णुर्गतिसत्तमः ॥ ६० ॥
verses.iast: bhagavān bhagahānandī vanamālī halāyudhaḥ, ādityō jyōtirādityaḥ sahiṣṇurgatisattamaḥ.

words.meaning: The origin, dissolution, the bondage and salvation of creatures, knowledge, ignorance – one who knows all these is Bhagavan.
One who withdraws the Bhagas, beginning with lordliness, into Himself at the time of dissolution.
One whose nature is Ananda (bliss).
One who wears the floral wreath (Vanamala) called Vaijayanti, which consists of the categories of five elements.
One who in His incarnation as Balabhadra had Hala or ploughshare as His weapon.
One who was born of Aditi in His incarnation as Vamana.
One who dwells in the brilliance of the sun's orb.
One who puts up with the contraries like heat and cold.
One who is the ultimate resort and support of all, and the greatest of all beings.

verses.devanagari: सुधन्वा खण्डपरशुर्दारुणो द्रविणप्रदः । दिवस्पृक् सर्वदृग्व्यासो वाचस्पतिरयोनिजः ॥ ६१ ॥
verses.iast: sudhanvā khaṇḍaparaśurdāruṇō draviṇapradaḥ, divaspṛk sarvadṛgvyāsō vācaspatirayōnijaḥ.

words.meaning: One who has got as His weapon the bow named Saranga of great excellence.
The battle-axe that destroys enemies.
One who is harsh and merciless to those who are on the evil path.
One who bestows the desired wealth on devotees.
One who touches the heavens.
One whose comprehension includes everything in its ambit.
The Lord is Vachaspati because He is the master of all learning. He is Ayonija because He was not born of a mother. This forms a noun in combination with the attribute.

verses.devanagari: त्रिसामा सामगः साम निर्वाणं भेषजं भिषक् । संन्यासकृच्छमश्यान्तो निष्ठा शान्तिः परायणम् ॥ ६२ ॥
verses.iast: trisāmā sāmagaḥ sāma nirvāṇaṁ bheṣajaṁ bhiṣak, saṁnyāsakṛcchamaśyāntō niṣṭhā śāntiḥ parāyaṇam.

words.meaning: One who is praised by the chanters of Sama-gana through the three Samas known as Devavratam.
One who chants the Sama-gana.
Among the Vedas, I am Sama Veda.
That in which all miseries cease and which is of the nature of supreme bliss.
The medicine for the disease of Samsara.
The Lord is called Bhishak or physician.
One who instituted the fourth Ashrama of Sanyasa for the attainment of Moksha.
One who has ordained the pacification of the mind as the most important discipline for Sannyasins (ascetics).
The peaceful, being without interest in pleasures of the world.
One in whom all beings remain in abeyance at the time of Pralaya.
One in whom there is complete erasing of Avidya or ignorance. That is Brahman.
The state, which is the highest and from which there is no return to lower states.

verses.devanagari: शुभाङ्गः शान्तिदः स्रष्टा कुमुदः कुवलेशयः । गोहितो गोपतिर्गोप्ता वृषभाक्षो वृषप्रियः ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.iast: śubhāṅgaḥ śāntidaḥ sraṣṭā kumudaḥ kuvaleśayaḥ, gōhitō gōpatirgōptā vṛṣabhākṣō vṛṣapriyaḥ.

words.meaning: One with a handsome form.
One who bestows shanti, that is, a state of freedom from attachment, antagonism, etc.
One who brought forth everything at the start of the creative cycle.
'Ku' means the earth. One who delights in it.

'Ku' means earth. That which surrounds it is water, so 'Kuvala' means water. One who lies in water is Kuvalesaya. 'Kuvala' also means the underside of serpents. One wholies on a serpent, known as Adisesha, is Kuvalesaya.
One who protected the cows by uplifting the mount Govardhana in His incarnation as Krishna.
The Lord of the earth is Vishnu.
One who is the protector of the earth. Or one who hides Himself by His Maya.
One whose eyes can rain all desirable objects on devotees. Vrushabha means Dharma and so one whose look is Dharma.
One to whom Vrusha or Dharma is dear.

verses.devanagari: अनिवर्ती निवृत्तात्मा संक्षेप्ता क्षेमकृच्छिवः । श्रीवत्सवक्षाः श्रीवासः श्रीपतिः श्रीमतां वरः ॥ ६४ ॥
verses.iast: anivartī nivṛttātmā saṁkṣeptā kṣemakṛcchivaḥ, śrīvatsavakṣāḥ śrīvāsaḥ śrīpatiḥ śrīmatāṁ varaḥ.

words.meaning: One who never retreats in the battle with Asuras. Or one who, being devoted to Dharma, never abandons it.
One whose mind is naturally withdrawn from the objects of senses.
One who at the time of cosmic dissolution contracts the expansive universe into a subtle state.
One who gives Kshema or protection to those that go to him.
One who purifies everyone by the very utterance of His name.
One on whose chest there is a mark called Shrivasta.
One on whose chest Shridevi always dwells.
One whom at the time of the churning of the Milk ocean Shridevi chose as her consort, rejecting all other Devas and Asuras. Or Shri mean supreme Cosmic Power. The Lord is the master of that Power.
One who is supreme over all deities like Brahma who are endowed with power and wealth of the Vedas.

verses.devanagari: श्रीदः श्रीशः श्रीनिवासः श्रीनिधिः श्रीविभावनः । श्रीधरः श्रीकरः श्रेयः श्रीमान् लोकत्रयाश्रयः ॥ ६५ ॥
verses.iast: śrīdaḥ śrīśaḥ śrīnivāsaḥ śrīnidhiḥ śrīvibhāvanaḥ, śrīdharaḥ śrīkaraḥ śreyaḥ śrīmān lōkatrayāśrayaḥ.

words.meaning: One who bestows prosperity on devotees.
One who is Lord of the Goddess Shri.
Shri here denotes men with Shri, that is, virtue and power. He who dwells in such men is Shrinivasa.
One who is the seat of all Shri, that is, virtues and powers.
One who grants every form of prosperity and virtue according to their Karma.
One who bears on His chest Shri who is the mother of all.
One who makes devotees – those who praise, think about Him and worship Him – into virtuous and powerful beings.
'Shreyas' means the attainment of what is un- decaying good and happiness. Such a state is the nature of the Lord.
One in whom there are all forms of Shri that is power, virtue, beauty etc.
One who is the support of all the three worlds.

verses.devanagari: स्वक्षः स्वङ्गः शतानङ्दो नङ्दिर्ज्योतिर्गणेश्वरः । विजितात्मा विधेयात्मा सत्कीर्तिश्छिन्नसंशयः ॥ ६६ ॥
verses.iast: svakṣaḥ svaṅgaḥ śatānaṅdō naṅdirjyōtirgaṇeśvaraḥ, vijitātmā vidheyātmā satkīrtiśchinnasaṁśayaḥ.

words.meaning: One who's Akshas (eyes) are handsome like lotus flowers.
One whose limbs are beautiful.
One who is non-dual and is of the nature of supreme bliss.
One who is of the nature of supreme Bliss.
One who is the Lord of the stars, that is, Jyotirgana.
One who has conquered the Atma that is the mind.
One whose form or nature cannot be determined as 'only this'.
One whose fame is of the nature of truth.
One who has no doubts, as everything is clear to him like a fruit in the palm.

verses.devanagari: उदीर्णः सर्वतश्चक्षुरनीशः शाश्वतस्थिरः । भूशयो भूषणो भूतिर्विशोकः शोकनाशनः ॥ ६७ ॥
verses.iast: udīrṇaḥ sarvataścakṣuranīśaḥ śāśvatasthiraḥ, bhūśayō bhūṣaṇō bhūtirviśōkaḥ śōkanāśanaḥ.

words.meaning: He who is superior to all beings.
One who, being of the nature of pure consciousness, can see everthing in all directions.
One who cannot have anyone to lord over him.
One, who though eternal is also unchanging.
One who, while seeking the means to cross over to Lanka, had to sleep on the ground of the sea-beach.
One who adorned the earth by manifesting as various incarnations.
One who is the abode or the essence of everthing, or is the source of all glorious manifestations.
One who, being of the nature of bliss, is free from all sorrow.
One who effaces the sorrows of devotees even by mere remembrance.

verses.devanagari: अर्चिष्मानर्चितः कुंभो विशुद्धात्मा विशोधनः । अनिरुद्धोप्रतिरथः प्रद्युम्नोमितविक्रमः ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.iast: arciṣmānarcitaḥ kuṁbhō viśuddhātmā viśōdhanaḥ, aniruddhōpratirathaḥ pradyumnōmitavikramaḥ.

words.meaning: He by whose rays of light (Archish), the sun, the moon and other bodies are endowed with rays of light.
One who is worshipped by Brahma and other Devas who are themselves the objects of worship in all the worlds.
He who contains in Himself every thing as in a pot.
Being above the three Gunas, Satva, Rajas and Tamas, the Lord is pure spirit and is also free from all impurities.
One who destroys all sins by mere remembrance.
The last one of the four Vyuhas – Vasudeva, Samkarshana, Pradyumna and Aniruddhaḥ. Or one who, cannot be obstructed by enemies.
One who has no Pratiratha or an equal antagonist to confront.
One whose Dyumna or wealth is of a superior and sacred order. Or one of the four Vyuhas.
One of unlimited prowess. Or one whose prowess cannot be obstructed by any one.

verses.devanagari: कालनेमिनिहा वीरः शौरिः शूरजनेश्वरः । त्रिलोकात्मा त्रिलोकेशः केशवः केशिहा हरिः ॥ ६९ ॥
verses.iast: kālaneminihā vīraḥ śauriḥ śūrajaneśvaraḥ, trilōkātmā trilōkeśaḥ keśavaḥ keśihā hariḥ.

words.meaning: One who destroyed the Asura named Kalanemi.
One who is courageous.
One who was born in the clan of Sura as Krishna.
One who by his overwhelming prowess controls even great powers like Indra and others.
One who in his capacity as the inner pervade is the soul for the three worlds.
One under whose guidance and command everything in the three words is functioning.
By Kesha is meant the rays of light spreading within the orbit of the sun.
One who destroyed the Asura named Keshi.
One who destroys Samsara, that is, entanglement in the cycle of birth and death along with ignorance, its cause.

verses.devanagari: कामदेवः कामपालः कामी कान्तः कृतागमः । अनिर्देश्यवपुर्विष्णुर्वीरोनन्तो धनञ्जयः ॥ ७० ॥
verses.iast: kāmadevaḥ kāmapālaḥ kāmī kāntaḥ kṛtāgamaḥ, anirdeśyavapurviṣṇurvīrōnantō dhanañjayaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is desired by persons in quest of the four values of life – Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha.
One who protects or assures the desired ends of people endowed with desires.
One who by nature has all his desires satisfied.

One whose form is endowed with great beauty. Or one who effects the 'Anta' or dissolution of 'Ka' or Brahma at the end of a Dviparardha (the period of Brahma's lifetime extending over a hundred divine years).
He who produced scriptures like Shruti, Smruti and Agama.
He is called so, because, being above the Gunas, His form cannot be determined.
One whose brilliance has spread over the sky and over the earth.
One who has the power of Gati or movement.
One who pervades everything, who is eternal, who is the soul of all, and who cannot be limited by space, time, location, etc.
Arjuna is called so because by his conquest of the kingdoms in the four quarters he acquired great wealth. Arjuna is a Vibhuti, a glorious manifestation of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: ब्रह्मण्यो ब्रह्मकृद्ब्रह्मा ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविवर्धनः । ब्रह्मविद्ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मी ब्रह्मज्ञो ब्राह्मणप्रियः ॥ ७१ ॥
verses.iast: brahmaṇyō brahmakṛdbrahmā brahma brahmavivardhanaḥ, brahmavidbrāhmaṇō brahmī brahmajñō brāhmaṇapriyaḥ.

words.meaning: The Vedas, Brahmanas and knowledge are indicated by the word Brahma. As the Lord promotes these, He is called Brahmanya.
One who performs Brahma or Tapas (austerity).
One who creates everything as the creator Brahma.
Being big expanding, the Lord who is known from indications like Satya (Truth), is called Brahma. Or Brahma is Truth, Knowledge and Infinity!
One who promotes Tapas (austerity), etc.
One who knows the Vedas and their real meaning.
One who, in the form of Brahmana, instructs the whole world, saying, 'It is commanded so and so in the Veda'.
One in whom is established such entities as Tapas, Veda, mind, Prana etc. which are parts of Brahma and which are also called Brahma.
One who knows the nature of Brahman.
One to whom holy men are devoted.

verses.devanagari: महाक्रमो महाकर्मा महातेजा महोरगः । महाक्रतुर्महायज्वा महायज्ञो महाहविः ॥ ७२ ॥
verses.iast: mahākramō mahākarmā mahātejā mahōragaḥ, mahākraturmahāyajvā mahāyajñō mahāhaviḥ.

words.meaning: One with enormous strides. May Vishnu with enormous strides bestow on us happiness.
One who is performing great works like the creation of the world.
He from whose brilliance, sun and other luminaries derive their brilliance. Or one who is endowed with the brilliance of various excellences.
He is also the great serpent.
He is the great Kratu or sacrifice.
One who is great and performs sacrifices for the good of the world.
He who is the great sacrifice.
The whole universe conceived as Brahman and offered as sacrificial offering (Havis) into the fire of the Self, which is Brahman.

verses.devanagari: स्तव्यः स्तवप्रियः स्तोत्रं स्तुतिः स्तोता रणप्रियः । पूर्णः पूरयिता पुण्यः पुण्यकीर्तिरनामयः ॥ ७३ ॥
verses.iast: stavyaḥ stavapriyaḥ stōtraṁ stutiḥ stōtā raṇapriyaḥ, pūrṇaḥ pūrayitā puṇyaḥ puṇyakīrtiranāmayaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is the object of laudations of everyone but who never praises any other being.
One who is pleased with hymns.
A Stotra means a hymn proclaiming the glory, attributes and names of the Lord.
A praise.
One who, being all -formed, is also the person who sings a hymn of praise.

One who is fond of fight for the protection of the world, and for the purpose always sports in His hands the five weapons, the discus Sudarshana, the mace Kaumodaki, the bow Saranga, and the sword Nandaka besides the conch Panchajanya.
One who is self-fulfilled, being the source of all powers and excellences.
One who is not only self-fulfilled but gives all fulfillments to others.
One by only hearing about whom all sins are erased.
One of holy fame. His excellences are capable of conferring great merit on others.
One who is not afflicted by any disease that is born of cause, internal or external.

verses.devanagari: मनोजवस्तीर्थकरो वसुरेता वसुप्रदः । वसुप्रदो वासुदेवो वसुर्वसुमना हविः ॥ ७४ ॥
verses.iast: manōjavastīrthakarō vasuretā vasupradaḥ, vasupradō vāsudevō vasurvasumanā haviḥ.

words.meaning: One who, being all pervading, is said to be endowed with speed likes that of the mind.
Tirtha means Vidya, a particular branch of knowledge or skill.
He whose Retas (Semen) is gold (Vasu).
One who gladly bestows wealth in abundance. He is really the master of all wealth, and others who seem to be so are in those positions only because of His grace.
One who bestows on devotees the highest of all wealth, namely Moksha.
The son of Vasudeva.
He in whom all creation dwells.
One whose mind dwells equally in all things.
Havis or sacrificial offerings.

verses.devanagari: सद्गतिः सत्कृतिः सत्ता सद्भूतिः सत्परायणः । शूरसेनो यदुश्रेष्ठः सन्निवासः सुयामुनः ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.iast: sadgatiḥ satkṛtiḥ sattā sadbhūtiḥ satparāyaṇaḥ, śūrasenō yaduśreṣṭhaḥ sannivāsaḥ suyāmunaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is attained by such persons. Or who is endowed with intelligence of great excellence.
One whose achievements are for the protection of the world.
Experience that is without any difference of an external nature from similar objects or dissimilar objects as also internal differences is called Satta.
The Paramatman who is pure existence and conscousness, who is unsublatable and who manifests Himself in many ways.
He who is the highest Status attainable by holy men who have realized the Truth.
One having an army of heroic wariours like Hanuman.
One who is the greatest among the Yadus.
One who is the resort of holy knowing ones.
One who is surrounded by may illustrious persons associated with the river Yamuna like Devaki, Vasudeva, Nandagopa, Yasoda, Balabhadra, Subhadra, etc.

verses.devanagari: भूतावासो वासुदेवः सर्वासुनिलयोनलः । दर्पहा दर्पदो दृप्तो दुर्धरोथापराजितः ॥ ७६ ॥
verses.iast: bhūtāvāsō vāsudevaḥ sarvāsunilayōnalaḥ, darpahā darpadō dṛptō durdharōthāparājitaḥ.

words.meaning: He in whom all the beings dwell.
The Divinity who covers the whole universe by Maya.
He in whose form as the Jiva all the vital energy or Prana of all living beings dissolves.
One whose wealth or power has no limits.
One who puts down the pride of persons who walk along the unrighteous path.
One who endows those who walk the path of righteousness with a sense of self-respect regarding their way of life.
One who is ever satisfied by the enjoyment of His own inherent bliss.
One who is very difficult to be borne orcontained in the heart in meditation.
One who is never conquered by internal enemies like attachment and by external enemies like Asuras.

verses.devanagari: विश्वमूर्तिर्महामूर्तिर्दीप्तमूर्तिरमूर्तिमान् । अनेकमूर्तिरव्यक्तः शतमूर्तिः शताननः ॥ ७७ ॥
verses.iast: viśvamūrtirmahāmūrtirdīptamūrtiramūrtimān, anekamūrtiravyaktaḥ śatamūrtiḥ śatānanaḥ.

words.meaning: One who, being the soul of all, has the whole universe as His body.
One with an enormous form stretched on a bedstead constituted of the serpent Adisesha.
One with a luminous form of knowledge.
He who is without a body born of Karma.
One who assumes several bodies in His incarnations as it pleases Him in or to help the world.
One who cannot be clearly described as 'This' even though He has many forms.
One who, though He is of the nature of Pure Consciousness, assumes different forms for temporary purposes.
He is called one with a hundred faces to indicate that He has several forms.

verses.devanagari: एको नैकः सवः कः किं यत्तत्पदमनुत्तमम् । लोकबन्धुर्लोकनाथो माधवो भक्तवत्सलः ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.iast: ekō naikaḥ savaḥ kaḥ kiṁ yattatpadamanuttamam, lōkabandhurlōkanāthō mādhavō bhaktavatsalaḥ.

words.meaning: One without any kind of differences that are internal or that relate to similar objects external or to dissimilar objects.
One who has numerous bodies born of Maya.
That Yajna in which Soma is made.
The syllable 'Ka' indicatesjoy or happiness. So it means one who is hymned as constituted of joy.
One who is fit to be contemplated upon, because He is the summation of all values.
One who is by nature existent. The word 'Yat' indicates a self-subsisting entity.
Brahma is so called because He 'expands'.
Braman is 'Pada' or Status, because He is the goal of all Moksha-seekers. It is Anuttama, because It is that beyond which there is nothing else to be attained.
One who is friend of the world.
One to whom all the worlds pray.
One who was born in the clan of Madhu.
One who has got love for devotees.

verses.devanagari: सुवर्णवर्णो हेमाङ्गो वराङ्गश्चन्दनाङ्गदी । वीरहा विषमः शून्यो घृताशीरचलश्चलः ॥ ७९ ॥
verses.iast: suvarṇavarṇō hemāṅgō varāṅgaścandanāṅgadī, vīrahā viṣamaḥ śūnyō ghṛtāśīracalaścalaḥ.

words.meaning: One who has got the colour of gold.
One whose form is like that of gold.
He the parts of whose form are brilliant.
One who is adorned with armlets that generate joy.
One who destroyed heroes (Viras) like Kiranyakashipu for protecting Dharma.
One to whom there is no euql because nothing is comparable to Him by any characteristic.
One who, being without any attributes, appears as Sunya (emptiness).
One whose blessings are unfailing.
One who cannot be deprived of His real nature as Truth, Intelligence and Infinity.
One who moves in the form of air.

verses.devanagari: अमानी मानदो मान्यो लोकस्वामी त्रिलोकधृत् । सुमेधा मेधजो धन्यः सत्यमेधा धराधरः ॥ ८० ॥
verses.iast: amānī mānadō mānyō lōkasvāmī trilōkadhṛt, sumedhā medhajō dhanyaḥ satyamedhā dharādharaḥ.

words.meaning: He who, being of the nature of Pure Consciousness, has no sense of identification with anything that is not Atman.

One who by His power of Maya induces the sense of self in non-self. Or one who has regard and beneficence towards devotees. Or one who destroys in the knowing ones the sense of identification with the non-self.
One who is to be adored by all, because He is the God of all.
One who is the Lord of all the fourteen spheres.
One who supports all the three worlds.
One with great and beneficent intelligence.
One who arose from Yaga (a kind of sacrifice).
One who has attained all His ends and therefore is self-satisfied.
One whose intelligence is fruitful.
One who supports the worlds by His fractiosn like Adisesha.

verses.devanagari: तेजोवृषो द्युतिधरः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः । प्रग्रहो निग्रहो व्यग्रो नैकशृङ्गो गदाग्रजः ॥ ८१ ॥
verses.iast: tejōvṛṣō dyutidharaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṁ varaḥ, pragrahō nigrahō vyagrō naikaśṛṅgō gadāgrajaḥ.

words.meaning: One who in the form of the sun causes rainfall at all times.
One whose form is always brilliant.
One who is superior to all bearing arms.
One who accepts the offerings of devotees with great delight.
One who controls and destroys everything.
One who has no Agra or end. Or one who is very attentive (Vyagra) in granting the prayers of devotees.
One with four horns.
One who is revealed first by Mantra (Nigada). Or one who is the elder brother of Gada.

verses.devanagari: चतुर्मूर्तिश्चतुर्बाहुश्चतुर्व्यूहश्चतुर्गतिः । चतुरात्मा चतुर्भावश्चतुर्वेदविदेकपात् ॥ ८२ ॥
verses.iast: caturmūrtiścaturbāhuścaturvyūhaścaturgatiḥ, caturātmā caturbhāvaścaturvedavidekapāt.

words.meaning: One with four aspects as Virat, Sutratma, Avyakruta, and Turiya. Or one with four horns with colours white, red, yellow and black.
One with four arms, as Vasudeva is always described.
One having four manifestations.
One who is sought as the end by the four Orders of life and four Varnas ordained by the scriptures.
One whose self is specially endowed with puissance, because it is without any attachment, antagonism, etc.
One from whom has originated the four human values – Dharma, Artha, Kama, and Moksha.
One who understands the true meaning of the four Vedas.
One with a single Pada, part or leg. Or one with a single foot or manifestation.

verses.devanagari: समावर्तो निवृत्तात्मा दुर्जयो दुरतिक्रमः । दुर्लभो दुर्गमो दुर्गो दुरावासो दुरारिहा ॥ ८३ ॥
verses.iast: samāvartō nivṛttātmā durjayō duratikramaḥ, durlabhō durgamō durgō durāvāsō durārihā.

words.meaning: One who effectively whirls the wheel of Samsara.
One who is not Nivruta (separated from) anything or anywhere, because He is all-pervading.
One who cannot be conquered.
One out of fear of whom, even heavenly objects like sun do not dare to oppose His command.
One who can be attained by Bhakti, which is difficult for a person to be endowed with.
One whom it is difficult to attain.
One the attainment of whom is rendered difficult by various obstructions.
He whom the Yogis with very great difficulty bring to reside in their hearts in Samadhi.
One who destroys beings like Asuras.

verses.devanagari: शुभाङ्गो लोकसारङ्गः सुतन्तुस्तन्तुवर्धनः । इन्द्रकर्मा महाकर्मा कृतकर्मा कृतागमः ॥ ८४ ॥
verses.iast: śubhāṅgō lōkasāraṅgaḥ sutantustantuvardhanaḥ, indrakarmā mahākarmā kṛtakarmā kṛtāgamaḥ.

words.meaning: One whose form is very auspicious to meditate upon.
One who like the Saranga (honey-beetle) grasps the essence of the world.
As this universe of infinite extension belongs to Him, the Lord is called Sutantu.
One who can augment or contract the web of this world.
One whose actions are like that of Indra, that is, are of a highly commendable nature.
One of whom the great elements like Akasha are effects.
One who has fulfilled everything and has nothing more to accomplish.
One who has given out the Agama in the shape of the Veda.

verses.devanagari: उद्भवः सुन्दरः सुन्दो रत्ननाभः सुलोचनः । अर्को वाजसनः शृङ्गी जयन्तः सर्वविज्जयी  ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.iast: udbhavaḥ sundaraḥ sundō ratnanābhaḥ sulōcanaḥ, arkō vājasanaḥ śṛṅgī jayantaḥ sarvavijjayī .

words.meaning: One who assumes great and noble embodiments out of His own will.
One who has a graceful attractiveness that surprises everyone.
One who is noted for extreme tenderness (Undanam).
Ratna indicates beauty; so one whose navel is very beautiful.
One who has brilliant eyes, that is, knowledge of everything.
One who is being worshipped even by beings like Brahma who are themselves objects of worship.
One who gives Vajam (food) to those who entreat Him.
One who at the time of Pralaya (cosmic dissolution) assumed the form of a fish having prominent antenna.
One who conquers enemies easily.
The Lord is 'Sarvavit' as He has knowledge of everything. He is 'Jayi' because He is the conqueror of all the inner forces like attachment, anger etc., as also of external foes like Hiranyaksha.

verses.devanagari: सुवर्णबिन्दुरक्षोभ्यः सर्ववागीश्वरेश्वरः । महाह्रदो महागर्तो महाभूतो महानिधिः ॥ ८६ ॥
verses.iast: suvarṇabindurakṣōbhyaḥ sarvavāgīśvareśvaraḥ, mahāhradō mahāgartō mahābhūtō mahānidhiḥ.

words.meaning: One whose 'Bindus' that is, limbs, are euaql to gold in brilliance.
One who is never perturbed by passions like attachment and aversion, by objects of the senses like sound, taste, etc., and by Asuras the antagonists of the Devas.
One who is the master of all masters of learning, including Brahma.
He is called a great Hrada (lake), because being the paramatman who is of the nature of Bliss, the Yogis who contemplate upon Him dip themselves in that lake of Bliss and attain to great joy.
One whose Maya is difficult to cross like a big pit.
One who is not divided by the three periods of time – past, present and future.
One in whom all the great elements have their support. He is Mahan or a great one and 'Nidhi', the most precious one.

verses.devanagari: कुमुदः कुन्दरः कुन्दः पर्जन्यः पावनोऽनिलः । अमृताशोमृतवपुः सर्वज्ञः सर्वतोमुखः ॥ ८७ ॥
verses.iast: kumudaḥ kundaraḥ kundaḥ parjanyaḥ pāvano’nilaḥ, amṛtāśōmṛtavapuḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvatōmukhaḥ.

words.meaning: 'Ku' means earth; one who gives joy (muda) to the earth by freeing it of its burdens is Kumuda.
One who offers blessings as pure as Kunda or jasmine.
One who has limbs as beautiful as Kunda or Jasmine.

The word means cloud. One who resembles the cloud in extinguishing the three Tapas (heats, that is, miseries) arising from psychological, material and spiritual causes. Or one who rains all desires like a cloud.
One by merely remembering whom a devotee attains purity.
'Ilanam' means inducement. One who is without any inducement is Anila. Ilana also means sleep. So one who sleeps not or is ever awake is Anila.
One who consumes Amruta or immortal bliss, which is His own nature.
One whose form is deathless, that is, undecaying.
One who is all-knowing.
One who has faces everywhere.

verses.devanagari: सुलभः सुव्रतः सिद्धः शत्रुजिच्छत्रुतापनः । न्यग्रोधोऽदुम्बरोऽश्वत्थश्चाणूरान्ध्रनिषूदनः ॥ ८८ ॥
verses.iast: sulabhaḥ suvrataḥ siddhaḥ śatrujicchatrutāpanaḥ, nyagrodho’dumbaro’śvatthaścāṇūrāndhraniṣūdanaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is attained easily by offering trifles like leaf, flower, and fruits etc., with devotion.
'Vratati' means enjoys. So, one who enjoys pure offerings. It can also mean one who is a non-enjoyer, that is, a mere witness.
One whose objects are always attained, that is, omnipotent and unobstructed by any other will.
Conqueror of all forces of evil.
One who destroys the enemies of the Devas.
That which remains above all and grows downward. That is, He is the source of everything that is manifest.
One who as the Supreme cause is 'above the sky', that is, superior to all.
That which does not last even for the next day.
One who destroyed a valiant fighter Chanura belonging to the race of Andhra.

verses.devanagari: सहस्रार्चिः सप्तजिह्वः सप्तैधाः सप्तवाहनः । अमूर्तिरनघोचिन्त्यो भयकृद्भयनाशनः ॥ ८९ ॥
verses.iast: sahasrārciḥ saptajihvaḥ saptaidhāḥ saptavāhanaḥ, amūrtiranaghōcintyō bhayakṛdbhayanāśanaḥ.

words.meaning: One with innumerable Archis or rays.
The Lord in his manifestation as Fire is conceived as having seven tongues of flame.
The Lord who is of the nature of fire has seven Edhas or forms of brilliance.
The Lord in the form of Surya or sun has seven horses as his vehicles or mounts.
One who is without sins or without sorrow.
One who is not determinable by any criteria of knowledge, being Himself the witnessing Self- certifying all knowledge.
One who is without sins or without sorrow.
One who generates fear in those who go along the evil path. Or one who cuts at the root of all fear.
One who destroys the fears of the virtuous.

verses.devanagari: अणुर्बृहत्कृशः स्थूलो गुणभृन्निर्गुणो महान् ।। अधृतस्स्वधृतस्वास्यः प्राग्वंशो वंशवर्धनः ॥ ९० ॥
verses.iast: aṇurbṛhatkṛśaḥ sthūlō guṇabhṛnnirguṇō mahān,| adhṛtassvadhṛtasvāsyaḥ prāgvaṁśō vaṁśavardhanaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is extremely subtle.
The huge and mighty.
One who is non-material.
Being the inner pervader of all, He is figuratively described as Stula or huge.

The support of the Gunas. He is so called because in the creative cycle of creation, sustentation, and dissolution, He is the support of the Gunas – Satva, Rajas and Tamas – with which these functions are performed.
One who is without the Gunas of Prakruti.
The great.
One who, being the support of all supporting agencies, like Pruthvi (Earth), is not supported by anything external to Him.
One supported by oneself.
One whose face is beautiful and slightly red like the inside of a lotus flower.
The family lines of others are preceded by the lines of still others, but the Lord's descendent, namely, the world system, is not preceded by anything else.
One who augments or destroys the world-system, which is His off-spring.

verses.devanagari: भारभृत् कथितो योगी योगीशः सर्वकामदः । आश्रमः श्रमणः । क्षामः सुपर्णो वायुवाहनः ॥ ९१ ॥
verses.iast: bhārabhṛt kathitō yōgī yōgīśaḥ sarvakāmadaḥ, āśramaḥ śramaṇaḥ, kṣāmaḥ suparṇō vāyuvāhanaḥ.

words.meaning: One who bears the weight of the earth assuming the form of Ananta.
One who is spoken of as the highest by the Veda or one of whom all Vedas speak.
Yoga here means knowledge. So He who is attained by that is Yogi. Or Yoga means Samadhi. He who is ever established in His own Self, that is, the Paramatma. He is therefore Yogi.
He who is never shaken from Yoga or knowledge and establishment in His own Self, unlike ordinary Yogis who slip away from Yoga on account of obstacles.
One who bestows all desired fruits.
One who is the bestower of rest on all who are wandering in the forest of Samsara.
One who brings tribulations to those who live without using their discriminative power.
He who brings about the decline of all beings.
The lord who has manifested Himself as the tree of Samsara has excellent leaves (Parna) in the form of Vedic passages (Chandas).
He for fear of whom Vayu (Air) carries all beings.

verses.devanagari: धनुर्धरो धनुर्वेदो दङ्डो दमयिता दमः । अपराजितस्सर्वसहो नियन्ता नियमो यमः ॥ ९२ ॥
verses.iast: dhanurdharō dhanurvedō daṅḍō damayitā damaḥ, aparājitassarvasahō niyantā niyamō yamaḥ.

words.meaning: He who as Rama wielded the great bow.
He who as the same Rama, the son of Dasharatha, was the master of the science of archery.
He who is discipline among the disciplinarians.
He who inflicts punishments on people as Yama and as king.
He who is in the form of self-descipline in men as a result of enforcement.
One who is never defeated by enemies.
One who is expert in all Karmas (works).
One who appoints every person to his respective duties.
One on whom there is no enforcement of any law, or above whom there can be no overlord to enforce anything, as He is the controller of everything.
One on whom Yama has no control, that is one who has no death.

verses.devanagari: सत्त्ववान् सात्त्विकः सत्यः सत्यधर्मपरायणः । अभिप्रायः प्रियार्होऽर्हः प्रियकृत् प्रितिवर्धनः ॥ ९३ ॥
verses.iast: sattvavān sāttvikaḥ satyaḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ, abhiprāyaḥ priyārho’rhaḥ priyakṛt pritivardhanaḥ.

words.meaning: One who has got the strengthening qualities like heroism, prowess, etc.
One who is established essentially in the Satva Guna.
One who is truly established in good people.
One who is present in truthfulness and righteousness in its many aspects.
The One who is sought after by those who seek the ultimate values of life (Purushartha).
The being to whom the objects that are dear to oneself, are fit to be offered.
One who deserves to be worshipped with all the ingredients and rites of worship like offerings, praise, prostration, etc.
One who is not only to be loved but who does what is good and dear to those who worship Him.
One who enhances the joys of devotees.

verses.devanagari: विहायसगतिर्ज्योतिः सुरुचिर्हुतभुग्विभुः । रविर्विरोचनः सूर्यः सविता रविलोचनः ॥ ९४ ॥
verses.iast: vihāyasagatirjyōtiḥ surucirhutabhugvibhuḥ, ravirvirōcanaḥ sūryaḥ savitā ravilōcanaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is the support of Vishupada.
One who is the light of self-luminous consciousness that reveals oneself as well as other things.
The Lord whose Ruchi i.e. brilliance or will, is of an attractive nature.
One who eats, that is, receives, whatever is offered to whatever deities (Devas) in all sacrifices.
One who dwells everywhere. Or one who is the master of all the three worlds.
One who absorbs all Rasas (fluids) in the form of the Sun.
One who shines in many ways.
One who generates Shri or brilliance in Surya. Or Agni (Fire) is what is called Surya.
One who brings forth (Prasava) all the worlds.
One having the sun as the eye.

verses.devanagari: अनन्तो हुतभुग्भोक्ता सुखदो नैकजोग्रजः । अनिर्विण्णः सदामर्षी लोकाधिष्ठानमद्भुतः ॥ ९५ ॥
verses.iast: anantō hutabhugbhōktā sukhadō naikajōgrajaḥ, anirviṇṇaḥ sadāmarṣī lōkādhiṣṭhānamadbhutaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is eternal, all-pervading and indeterminable by space and time.
One who consumes what is offered in fire sacrifices.
One to whom the unconscious Prakruti is the object for enjoyment.
One who bestows liberation (Miksha) on devotees.
One who takes on birth again and again for the preservation of Dharma.
One who was born before everything else, that is, Hiranyagarbha.
One who is free from all sorrow, because he has secured all his desires and has no obstruction in the way of such achievement.
One who is always patient towards good men.
Brahman who, though without any other support for Himself, supports all the three worlds.
The wonderful being.

verses.devanagari: सनात्सनातनतमः कपिलः कपिरव्ययः । स्वस्तिदः स्वस्तिकृत्स्वस्ति स्वस्तिभुक्स्वस्तिदक्षिणः ॥ ९६ ॥
verses.iast: sanātsanātanatamaḥ kapilaḥ kapiravyayaḥ, svastidaḥ svastikṛtsvasti svastibhuksvastidakṣiṇaḥ.

words.meaning: The word Sanat indicates a great length of time. Time also is the manifestation of the Supreme Being.
Being the cause of all, He is more ancient than Brahma and other beings, who are generally considered eternal.
A subterranean fire in the ocean is Kapila, light red in colour.
'Ka' means water. One who drinks or absorbs all water by his Kapi, that is, the sun.
One in whom all the worlds get dissolved in Pralaya.
One who gives what is auspicious to devotees.
One who works bestowing what is good.
One whose auspicious form is characterized by supreme Bliss.
One who enjoys the Svasti mentioned above or who preserves the Svasti of devotees.
One who augments as Svasti (auspiciousness).

verses.devanagari: अरौद्रः कुन्डली चक्री विक्रम्यूर्जितशासनः । शब्दातिगः शब्दसहः शिशिरः शर्वरीकरः ॥ ९७ ॥
verses.iast: araudraḥ kunḍalī cakrī vikramyūrjitaśāsanaḥ, śabdātigaḥ śabdasahaḥ śiśiraḥ śarvarīkaraḥ.

words.meaning: Action, attachment and anger these three are Raudra. The Lord is one whose desires are all accomplished, so He has no attachment or aversion. So He is free from the Raudras mentioned above.
One who has taken the form of Adisesha.
One who sports in his hand the discus named Sudarshana, which is the category known as Manas, for the protection of all the worlds.
Vikrama means taking a stride, as also courage.
One whose dictates in the form of shrutis and smrutis are of an extremely sublime nature.
One who cannot be denoted by any sound because He has none of the characteristics, which could be grasped by sound.
One who is the purport of all Vedas.
One who is the shelter to those who are bruning in the three types of wordly fires – sufferings arising from material causes, psychological causes and spiritual causes.

For those in bondage, the Atman is like Sarvari (night) and for an enlightened one the state of samsara is like night (Sarvari). So the Lord is called the one who generates Sarvari or night for both the enlightened and the bound ones.

verses.devanagari: अक्रूरः पेशलो दक्षो दक्षिणः । क्षमिणां वरः । विद्वत्तमो वीतभयः पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तनः ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.iast: akrūraḥ peśalō dakṣō dakṣiṇaḥ, kṣamiṇāṁ varaḥ, vidvattamō vītabhayaḥ puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is without cruelty.
One who is handsome in regard to His actions, mind, word and body.
One who is fullgrown, strong and does every thing quickly, such a person is Daksha.
This word is also means the same as the above Nama.
The greatest among the patient ones, because He is more patient than all Yogis noted for patience.
He who has got the unsurpassable and all- inclusive knowledge of everything.
One who, being eternally free and the Lord of all, is free from the fear of trnsmigratory life.
One to hear about whom and to sing of whom is meritorious.

verses.devanagari: उत्तारणो दुष्कृतिहा पुण्यो दुःस्वप्ननाशनः । वीरहा रक्षणस्सन्तो जीवनः पर्यवस्थितः ॥ ९९ ॥
verses.iast: uttāraṇō duṣkṛtihā puṇyō duḥsvapnanāśanaḥ, vīrahā rakṣaṇassantō jīvanaḥ paryavasthitaḥ.

words.meaning: One who takes beings over to the other shore of the ocean of Samsara.
One who effaces the evil effects of evil actions. Or one who destroys those who perform evil.
One who bestows holiness on those who remember and adore Him.
When adored and meditated upon, He saves one from dreams foreboding danger. Hence He is called so.
One who frees Jivas from bondage and thus saves them from the various transmigratory paths by bestowing liberation on them.
One who, assuming the Satvaguna, protects all the three worlds.
Those who adopt the virtuous path are called good men (Santah).
One who supports the lives of all beings as Prana.
One who remains pervading everywhere in this universe.

verses.devanagari: अनन्तरूपोनन्तश्रीर्जितमन्युर्भयापहः । चतुरश्रो गभीरात्मा विदिशो व्यादिशो दिशः ॥ १०० ॥
verses.iast: anantarūpōnantaśrīrjitamanyurbhayāpahaḥ, caturaśrō gabhīrātmā vidiśō vyādiśō diśaḥ.

words.meaning: One who has innumerable forms, as He dwells in this all-comprehending universe.
One whose Shri (glory) is infinite.
One who has overcome anger.
One who destroys the fears of beings from Samsara.
One who is just, because He bestows on Jivas the fruits of their Karma.
One whose nature is unfathomable.
One who distributes various furits of actions to persons differing in their forms according to competency.
One who gives to Indra and other deities directions according to their varied functions.
One who in the form of the Vedas bestows the fruits of their ritualistic actions on different beings.

verses.devanagari: अनादिर्भूर्भुवो लक्ष्मीस्सुवीरो रुचिराङ्गदः । जननो जनजन्मादिर्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः ॥ १०१ ॥
verses.iast: anādirbhūrbhuvō lakṣmīssuvīrō rucirāṅgadaḥ, jananō janajanmādirbhīmō bhīmaparākramaḥ.

words.meaning: One who has no beginning because He is the ultimate cause of all.
'Bhu' means support. One who is the support (Bhu) of even the earth, which is known to support all things.
He who is the bestower of all that is auspicious to the earth besides being its supporter.
One who has many brilliant ways of manifestation.
One who has very attractive armlets.
One who gives brith to living beings.
One who is the root cause of the origin of Jivas that come to have embodiment.
One who is the cause of fear.
One whose power and courage in His incarnations were a cause of fear for the Asuras.

verses.devanagari: आधारनिलयोधाता पुष्पहासः प्रजागरः । ऊर्ध्वगस्सत्पथाचारः प्राणदः प्रणवः पणः ॥ १०२ ॥
verses.iast: ādhāranilayōdhātā puṣpahāsaḥ prajāgaraḥ, ūrdhvagassatpathācāraḥ prāṇadaḥ praṇavaḥ paṇaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is the support of even all the basic supporting factors like the five elements – Ether, Air, Fire, Water and Earth.
One who is one's own support and therefore does not require another support.
One whose manifestation as the universe resembles the Hasa or blooming of buds into flowers.
One who is particularly awake, because He is eternal Awareness.
One who is above everything.
One who follows the conduct of the good.
One who givesback life to dead ones as in the case of Parikshit.
Pranava (Om) the manifesting sound symbol of Brahman. As He is inseparably related with Pranava, He is called Pranava.
It comes from the root 'Prana' meaning transaction. So one who bestows the fruits of Karma on all according to their Karma.

verses.devanagari: प्रमाणं प्राणनिलयः प्राणभृत् प्राणजीवनः । तत्त्वं तत्त्वविदेकात्मा जन्ममृत्युजरातिगः ॥ १०३ ॥
verses.iast: pramāṇaṁ prāṇanilayaḥ prāṇabhṛt prāṇajīvanaḥ, tattvaṁ tattvavidekātmā janmamṛtyujarātigaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is self-certifying, as He is Pure Consciousness.
The home or dissolving ground of the Pranas.
One who strengthens the Pranas as food (Anna).
He who keeps alive human beings with Vayus (airs) known as Prana, Apana etc.
Means Brahman, just as words like Amruta, Satya, Paramartha, etc.
One who knowns His own true nature.
One who is the sole being and the spirit (Atma) in all.
One who subsists without being subject to the six kinds of transformations – being born, existing, temporarily, growing, transforming, decaying and dying.

verses.devanagari: भूर्भुवःस्वस्तरुस्तारः सविता प्रपितामहः । यज्ञो यज्ञपतिर्यज्वा यज्ञाङ्गो यज्ञवाहनः ॥ १०४ ॥
verses.iast: bhūrbhuvaḥsvastarustāraḥ savitā prapitāmahaḥ, yajñō yajñapatiryajvā yajñāṅgō yajñavāhanaḥ.

words.meaning: The three Vyahrutis Bhuh, Bhuvah, Svah are said to be the essence of the Veda.
One who helps Jivas to go across the ocean of Samsara.
He who generates all the worlds.
One who is the father of Brahma and therefore the grandfather of all.
One who is of the form of Yajna.
One who is the protector and the master of the Yajnas.
One who manifests as the performer of a Yajna.
All the parts of His body as the incarnate Cosmic Boar are identified with the parts of a yajna.
One who supports the Yajna which yield various fruits.

verses.devanagari: यज्ञभृद्यज्ञकृद्यज्ञी यज्ञभुग्यज्ञसाधनः । यज्ञान्तकृद्यज्ञगुह्यमन्नमन्नाद एव च ॥ १०५ ॥
verses.iast: yajñabhṛdyajñakṛdyajñī yajñabhugyajñasādhanaḥ, yajñāntakṛdyajñaguhyamannamannāda eva ca.

words.meaning: He is so called, because He is the protector and supporter of all Yajna.
One who performs Yajna at the beginnig and end of the world.
One who is the Principal.
One who is the enjoyer of Yajna or Protector of Yajna.
One to whom the Yagya is the approach.
One who is the end or the fruits of Yajna.
The Gyana Yajna or the sacrifice of knowledge, which is the esoteric (Guhyam) of all the Yajnams.
That which is eaten by living beings. Or He who eats all beings.
One who is the eater of the whole world as food. The word Eva is added to show that He is also Anna, the food eaten.

verses.devanagari: आत्मयोनिः स्वयंजातो वैखानः सामगायनः । देवकीनन्दनः स्रष्टा क्षितीशः पापनाशनः ॥ १०६ ॥
verses.iast: ātmayōniḥ svayaṁjātō vaikhānaḥ sāmagāyanaḥ, devakīnandanaḥ sraṣṭā kṣitīśaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ.

words.meaning: One who is the source of all; that is, there is no material cause other than Himself for the universe.
He is also the instrumental cause.
One who excavated the earth, taking a unique form.
One who recites the Sama chants.
The Son of Devaki in the incarnation as Krishna.
The creator of all the worlds.
A master of the world. Here it denotes Rama.
He who destroys the sins of those who adore Him, meditate upon Him, remember and sing hymns of praise on Him.

verses.devanagari: शङ्खभृन्नन्दकी चक्री शार्ङ्गधन्वा गदाधरः । रथाङ्गपाणिरक्षोभ्यः सर्वप्रहरणायुधः ॥ १०७ ॥
verses.iast: śaṅkhabhṛnnandakī cakrī śārṅgadhanvā gadādharaḥ, rathāṅgapāṇirakṣōbhyaḥ sarvapraharaṇāyudhaḥ.
verses.meaning: sarvapraharaṇāyudha oṃ nama iti.

words.meaning: One who sports the conch known as Panchajanya, which stands for Tamasahamkara, of which the five elements are born.
One who has in His hand the sword known as Nandaka, which stands for Vidya (spiritual illumination).
One who sports the discus known as Sudarshana, which stands for the Rajasahamkara, out of which the Indriyas have come.
One who aims His Sarnga bow.
One who has the mace known as the Kaumodaki, which stands for the category of Buddhi.
One in whose hand is a wheel (Chakra).
One who cannot be upset by anything, because He controls all the above-mentioned weapons.
There is no rule that the Lord has got only the above- mentioned weapons. All things, which can be used for contacting or striking, are His weapons.

verses.devanagari: वनमाली गदी शार्ङ्गी शङ्खी चक्री च नन्दकी । श्रीमान् नारायणो विष्णुर्वासुदेवोभिरक्षतु ॥ १०८ ॥
verses.iast: vanamālī gadī śārṅgī śaṅkhī cakrī ca nandakī, śrīmān nārāyaṇō viṣṇurvāsudevōbhirakṣatu.
verses.meaning: śrī vāsudevo’bhirakṣatu oṃ nama iti. Protect us Oh Lord Narayana Who wears the forest garland, Who has the mace, conch, sword and the wheel. And who is called Vishnu and the Vasudeva.

sections.label: Phalaśruti
sections.note: What the recitation is said to bring, and the closing salutations.

verses.devanagari: उत्तरन्यासः भीष्म उवाच — इतीदं कीर्तनीयस्य केशवस्य महात्मनः । नाम्नां सहस्रं दिव्यानामशेषेण प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ १ ॥
verses.iast: uttaranyāsaḥ bhīṣma uvāca — itīdaṁ kīrtanīyasya keśavasya mahātmanaḥ, nāmnāṁ sahasraṁ divyānāmaśeṣeṇa prakīrtitam
verses.meaning: Bhishma said: Thus was told, all the holy thousand names of Kesava, who is great.

verses.devanagari: य इदं शृणुयान्नित्यं यश्चापि परिकीर्तयेत् । नाशुभं प्राप्नुयात् किञ्चित् सोमुत्रेह च मानवः ॥ २ ॥
verses.iast: ya idaṁ śṛṇuyānnityaṁ yaścāpi parikīrtayet, nāśubhaṁ prāpnuyāt kiñcit sōmutreha ca mānavaḥ.
verses.meaning: He who hears this daily and whoever recites it shall not attain to any evil, he shall be protected in this world and in the next.

verses.devanagari: वेदान्तगो ब्राह्मणः स्यात् क्षत्रियो विजयी भवेत् । वैश्यो धनसमृद्धः स्याच्छूद्रः सुखमवाप्नुयात् ॥ ३ ॥
verses.iast: vedāntagō brāhmaṇaḥ syāt kṣatriyō vijayī bhavet, vaiśyo dhanasamṛddhaḥ syācchūdraḥ sukhamavāpnuyāt.
verses.meaning: The Brahmin will get knowledge, the Kshatriya will get victory, the Vaisya will get wealth, the Shudra will get pleasures by reading these.

verses.devanagari: धर्मार्थी प्राप्नुयाद्धर्मम् अर्थार्थी चार्थमाप्नुयात् । कामानवाप्नुयात्कामी प्रजार्थी प्राप्नुयात्प्रजाम् ॥ ४ ॥
verses.iast: dharmārthī prāpnuyāddharmam arthārthī cārthamāpnuyāt. kāmānavāpnuyātkāmī prajārthī prāpnuyātprajām.
verses.meaning: He who seeks righteousness obtains righteousness, and he who seeks wealth obtains wealth; he who seeks progeny obtains his desires.

verses.devanagari: भक्तिमान् यः सदोत्थाय शुचिस्तद्गतमानसः । सहस्रं वासुदेवस्य नाम्नामेतत् रकीर्तयेत् ॥ ५ ॥
verses.iast: bhaktimān yaḥ sadōtthāya śucistadgatamānasaḥ, sahasraṁ vāsudevasya nāmnāmetat rakīrtayet.
verses.meaning: Whichever devoted man, getting up early in the morning and purifying himself, repeats this hymn devoted to Vasudeva, with a mind that is concentrated on Him...

verses.devanagari: यशः प्राप्नोति विपुलं याति प्राधान्यमेव च । अचलां श्रियमाप्नोति श्रेयः प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥ ६ ॥
verses.iast: yaśaḥ prāpnōti vipulaṁ yāti prādhānyameva ca, acalāṁ śriyamāpnōti śreyaḥ prāpnōtyanuttamam.
verses.meaning: That man attains to great fame, leadership among his peers, wealth that is secure and the supreme good unsupassed by anything...

verses.devanagari: न भयं क्वचिदाप्नोति वीर्यं तेजश्च विंदति । भवत्यरोगो द्युतिमान् बलरूपगुणान्वितः ॥ ७ ॥
verses.iast: na bhayaṁ kvacidāpnōti vīryaṁ tejaśca viṁdati, bhavatyarōgō dyutimān balarūpaguṇānvitaḥ.
verses.meaning: He will be free from all fears and be endowed with great courage and energy and he will be free from diseases.

verses.devanagari: रोगार्तो मुच्यते रोगाद्बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात् । भयान्मुच्येत भीतस्तु मुच्येतापन्न आपदः ॥ ८ ॥
verses.iast: rōgārtō mucyate rōgādbaddhō mucyeta bandhanāt, bhayānmucyeta bhītastu mucyetāpanna āpadaḥ.
verses.meaning: Beauty of form, strength of body and mind, and virtuous character will be natural to him.

verses.devanagari: दुर्गाण्यतितरत्याशु पुरुषः पुरुषोत्तमम् । स्तुवन्नामसहस्रेण नित्यं भक्तिसमन्वितः ॥ ९ ॥
verses.iast: durgāṇyatitaratyāśu puruṣaḥ puruṣōttamam, stuvannāmasahasreṇa nityaṁ bhaktisamanvitaḥ.
verses.meaning: A man quickly crosses over difficulties by praising the Supreme Person with a thousand names, ever accompanied by devotion.

verses.devanagari: वासुदेवाश्रयो मर्त्यो वासुदेवपरायणः । सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा याति ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥ १० ॥
verses.iast: vāsudevāśrayō martyō vāsudevaparāyaṇaḥ, sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā yāti brahma sanātanam.
verses.meaning: A mortal who takes refuge in Vāsudeva and is devoted to Vāsudeva, purified of all sins, attains to the eternal Brahman.

verses.devanagari: न वासुदेवभक्तानामशुभं विद्यते क्वचित् । जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिभयं नैवोपजायते ॥ ११ ॥
verses.iast: na vāsudevabhaktānāmaśubhaṁ vidyate kvacit, janmamṛtyujarāvyādhibhayaṁ naivōpajāyate.
verses.meaning: There is nothing inauspicious for the devotees of Vāsudeva. They are not afraid of birth, death, old age or disease.

verses.devanagari: इमं स्तवमधीयानः श्रद्धाभक्तिसमन्वितः । युज्येतात्मासुखक्षाम्तिश्रीधृतिस्मृतिकीर्तिभिः ॥ १२ ॥
verses.iast: imaṁ stavamadhīyānaḥ śraddhābhaktisamanvitaḥ, yujyetātmāsukhakṣāmtiśrīdhṛtismṛtikīrtibhiḥ.
verses.meaning: One who studies this hymn with faith and devotion will be endowed with happiness, forbearance, prosperity, patience, memory and fame.

verses.devanagari: न क्रोधो न च मात्सर्यं न लोभो नाशुभा मतिः । भवन्ति कृतपुण्यानां भक्तानां पुरुषोत्तमे ॥ १३ ॥
verses.iast: na krōdhō na ca mātsaryaṁ na lōbhō nāśubhā matiḥ, bhavanti kṛtapuṇyānāṁ bhaktānāṁ puruṣōttame.
verses.meaning: The devotee of the Lord Purushottama, has neither anger nor fear, nor avarice and nor bad thoughts.

verses.devanagari: द्यौस्सचन्द्रार्कनक्षत्रा खं दिशो भूर्महोदधिः । वासुदेवस्य वीर्येण विधृतानि महात्मनः ॥ १४ ॥
verses.iast: dyaussacandrārkanakṣatrā khaṁ diśō bhūrmahōdadhiḥ, vāsudevasya vīryeṇa vidhṛtāni mahātmanaḥ.
verses.meaning: The heavens, the moon, the sun, the stars, the sky, the directions, the earth and the ocean are sustained by the might of the great soul Vasudeva.

verses.devanagari: ससुरासुरगन्धर्वं सयक्षोरगराक्षसम् । जगद्वशे वर्ततेदं कृष्णस्य सचराचरम् ॥ १५ ॥
verses.iast: sasurāsuragandharvaṁ sayakṣōragarākṣasam, jagadvaśe vartatedaṁ kṛṣṇasya sacarācaram.
verses.meaning: All this world, that which moves and moves not, and which has Devas, Rakshasas and Gandharwas, and also Asuras and Nagas, are under the control of Lord Krishna.

verses.devanagari: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिः सत्त्वं तेजो बलं धृतिः । वासुदेवात्मकान्याहुः । क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञ एव च ॥ १६ ॥
verses.iast: indriyāṇi manō buddhiḥ sattvaṁ tejō balaṁ dhṛtiḥ, vāsudevātmakānyāhuḥ, kṣetraṁ kṣetrajña eva ca.
verses.meaning: The senses, mind, intellect, Sattva, splendour, strength and patience are said to be composed of Vasudeva, the field and the knower of the field.

verses.devanagari: सर्वागमानामाचारः प्रथमं परिकल्य्पते । आचारप्रभवो धर्मो धर्मस्य प्रभुरच्युतः ॥ १७ ॥
verses.iast: sarvāgamānāmācāraḥ prathamaṁ parikalypate, ācāraprabhavō dharmō dharmasya prabhuracyutaḥ.
verses.meaning: The conduct of all the Vedas is first conceived as the origin of conduct, the Dharma, the Lord of Dharma, the infallible.

verses.devanagari: ऋषयः पितरो देवा महाभूतानि धातवः । जङ्गमाजङ्गमं चेदं जगन्नारायणोद्भवम् ॥ १८ ॥
verses.iast: ṛṣayaḥ pitarō devā mahābhūtāni dhātavaḥ, jaṅgamājaṅgamaṁ cedaṁ jagannārāyaṇōdbhavam.
verses.meaning: The sages, the forefathers, the gods, the great beings, the metals, the movable and the immovable, this universe is born of Narayana.

verses.devanagari: योगो ज्ञानं तथा सांख्यं विद्याः शिल्पादिकर्म च । वेदाश्शास्त्राणि विज्ञानमेतत्सर्वं जनार्दनात् ॥ १९ ॥
verses.iast: yōgō jñānaṁ tathā sāṁkhyaṁ vidyāḥ śilpādikarma ca, vedāśśāstrāṇi vijñānametatsarvaṁ janārdanāt.
verses.meaning: Yoga, knowledge and also Sāṅkhya, the sciences, crafts and other actions, the Vedas, the scriptures and knowledge, all this comes from Janardana.

verses.devanagari: एको विष्णुर्महद्भूतं पृथग्भूतान्यनेकशः । त्रीन्–लोकान्व्याप्य भूतात्मा भुङ्क्ते विश्वभुगव्ययः ॥ २० ॥
verses.iast: ekō viṣṇurmahadbhūtaṁ pṛthagbhūtānyanekaśaḥ, trīn–lōkānvyāpya bhūtātmā bhuṅkte viśvabhugavyayaḥ.
verses.meaning: Vishnu alone, the Great Being, pervading the three worlds with many separate beings, the Soul of beings, enjoys the expanse of the Enjoyer of the universe.

verses.devanagari: इमं स्तवं भगवतो विष्णोर्व्यासेन कीर्तितम् । पठेद्य इच्छेत्पुरुषः श्रेयः प्राप्तुं सुखानि च ॥ २१ ॥
verses.iast: imaṁ stavaṁ bhagavatō viṣṇōrvyāsena kīrtitam, paṭhedya icchetpuruṣaḥ śreyaḥ prāptuṁ sukhāni ca.
verses.meaning: Any man who desires to attain prosperity and happiness should recite this hymn of Lord Vishnu recited by Vyasa.

verses.devanagari: विश्वेश्वरमजं देवं जगतः प्रभवाप्ययम् । भजन्ति ये पुष्कराक्षं न ते यान्ति पराभवम् ॥ २२ ॥
verses.iast: viśveśvaramajaṁ devaṁ jagataḥ prabhavāpyayam, bhajanti ye puṣkarākṣaṁ na te yānti parābhavam.
verses.meaning: na te yānti parābhavam oṃ nama iti. Those who worship the lotus-eyed Lord of the universe, the unborn God, the Lord of the universe, the inexhaustible, do not get defeated.

verses.devanagari: अर्जुन उवाच । पद्मपत्रविशालाक्ष पद्मनाभ सुरोत्तम । भक्तानामनुरक्तानां त्राता भव जनार्दन ॥ २३ ॥
verses.iast: arjuna uvāca: padmapatraviśālākṣa padmanābha surottama, bhaktānāmanuraktānāṃ trātā bhava janārdana.
verses.meaning: Om Namah Arjuna said — O lotus-petalled, large-eyed, lotus- naveled, best of the gods, be the savior of the devotees who are devoted to you, O Janardana.

verses.devanagari: श्री भगवानुवाच । यो मां नामसहस्रेण स्तोतुमिच्छति पांडव । सोहमेकेन श्लोकेन स्तुत एव न संशयः ॥ २४ ॥
verses.iast: śrī bhagavānuvāca: yō māṁ nāmasahasrēṇa stōtumicchati pāṁḍava, sōhamēkēna ślōkēna stuta ēva na saṁśayaḥ.
verses.meaning: stuta eva na saṃśaya oṃ nama iti The Lord said: He who likes, Oh Arjuna, to sing my praise, using these thousand names, should know Arjuna, that I would be satisfied By his singing of even one stanza, without any doubt. Om Nama, without any doubt.

verses.devanagari: व्यास उवाच । वासनाद्वासुदेवस्य वासितं ते जगत्रयम् । सर्वभूतनिवासोसि वासुदेव नमोस्तु ते ॥ २५ ॥
verses.iast: vyāsa uvāca: vāsanādvāsudēvasya vāsitaṁ tē jagatrayam, sarvabhūtanivāsōsi vāsudēva namōstu tē.
verses.meaning: śrīvāsudēva namōstuta ōṁ nama iti. Vyasa said: My salutations to you Vasudeva, because you who live in all the worlds make these worlds as places where beings live, and also Vasudeva, You live in all beings as their soul. Om Nama salutations to Vasudeva.

verses.devanagari: पार्वत्युवाच । केनोपायेन लघुना विष्णोर्नामसहस्रकम् । पठ्यते पंडितैर्नित्यं श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं प्रभो ॥ २६ ॥
verses.iast: pārvatyuvāca: kēnōpāyēna laghunā viṣṇōrnāmasahasrakam, paṭhyatē paṁḍitairnityaṁ śrōtumicchāmyahaṁ prabhō.
verses.meaning: Parvathi said: I am desirous to know, Oh Lord, how the scholars of this world will chant without fail these thousand names, by a method that is easy and quick.

verses.devanagari: ईश्वर उवाच । रीराम राम रामेति रमे रामे मनोरमे । सहस्रनामतत्तुल्यं रामनाम वरानने ॥ २७ ॥
verses.iast: īśvara uvāca: rīrāma rāma rāmēti ramē rāmē manōramē, sahasranāmatattulyaṁ rāmanāma varānanē.
verses.meaning: śrī rāmanāma varānana ōṁ nama iti. Lord Shiva said: Hey beautiful one, I play with Rama always, by chanting Rama Rama and Rama. Hey lady with a beautiful face, chanting of the name Rama, is same as the thousand names. Om Nama Rama Nama Rama.

verses.devanagari: ब्रह्मोवाच । नमोस्त्वनंताय सहस्रमूर्तये सहस्रपादाक्षिशिरोरुबाहवे । सहस्रनाम्ने पुरुषाय शाश्वते सहस्रकोटियुगधारिणे नमः ॥ २८ ॥
verses.iast: brahmōvāca: namōstvanaṁtāya sahasramūrtayē sahasrapādākṣiśirōrubāhavē, sahasranāmnē puruṣāya śāśvatē sahasrakōṭiyugadhāriṇē namaḥ.
verses.meaning: sahasrakōṭiyugadhāriṇē nama ōṁ nama iti. Brahma said: Salutations to Thee, Oh lord, Who runs the immeasurable time of thousands of crore yugas, Who has no end, Who has a thousand names, Who has a thousand forms, Who has a thousand feet, Who has a thousand eyes, Who has a thousand heads, Who has a thousand arms, and Who is always there. Om Nama He who runs thousands of crore yugas.

verses.devanagari: सन्जय उवाच । यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः । तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥ २९ ॥
verses.iast: sanjaya uvāca: yatra yōgēśvaraḥ kr̥ṣṇō yatra pārthō dhanurdharaḥ, tatra śrīrvijayō bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya said: Where Krishna, the king of Yogas, and where the wielder of bow, Arjuna, is there, there will exist all the good, all the the victory, all the fame, and all the justice in this world.

verses.devanagari: श्रीभगवानुवाच । अनन्याश्चिंतयंतो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥ ३० ॥
verses.iast: śrībhagavānuvāca: ananyāściṁtayaṁtō māṁ yē janāḥ paryupāsatē, tēṣāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ yōgakṣēmaṁ vahāmyaham.
verses.meaning: Sri Bhagavan said: I would take care of worries and cares of him who thinks and serves Me without any other thoughts.

verses.devanagari: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् । धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे ॥ ३१ ॥
verses.iast: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśāya ca duṣkr̥tām, dharmasaṁsthāpanārthāya saṁbhavāmi yugē yugē.
verses.meaning: I save the righteous and destroy the wicked, and establish righteousness in every age.

verses.devanagari: आर्ता विषण्णाः शिथिलाश्च भीताः घोरेषु च व्याधिषु वर्तमानाः । संकीर्त्य नारायणशब्दमात्रं विमुक्तदुःखाः सुखिनो भवंति ॥ ३२ ॥
verses.iast: ārtā viṣaṇṇāḥ śithilāśca bhītāḥ ghōrēṣu ca vyādhiṣu vartamānāḥ, saṁkīrtya nārāyaṇaśabdamātraṁ vimuktaduḥkhāḥ sukhinō bhavaṁti.
verses.meaning: If he who is worried, sad, broken, afraid, severely ill, if he who has heard tidings bad, sings Narayana and Narayana, all his cares would be taken care of.

verses.devanagari: कायेन वाचा मनसेंद्रियैर्वा बुध्यात्मना वा प्रकृतेः स्वभावात् । करोमि यद्यत् सकलं परस्मै नारायणायेति समर्पयामि ॥ ३३ ॥
verses.iast: kāyena vācā manaseṃdriyairvā budhyātmanā vā prakṛteḥ svabhāvāt, karomi yadyat sakalaṃ parasmai nārāyaṇāyeti samarpayāmi.
verses.meaning: Whatever I do either by body, speech, mind or sensory organs, either with my personal knowledge or natural trait, I surrender and submit all to that to supreme divine Narayana.

verses.devanagari: इति श्रीविष्णोर्दिव्यसहस्रनामस्तोत्रं सम्पूर्णम् । ॐ तत् सत्
verses.iast: iti śrīviṣṇordivyasahasranāmastotraṃ sampūrṇam. oṃ tat sat.
verses.meaning: This is the complete Divya Sahasranama Stotram of Sri Vishnu. Om Tat Sat.
